stem: According to the Preamble of the 1987 Constitution, who "ordain and promulgate this Constitution"?
choices: The Supreme Court of the Philippines
hints: The Preamble is the opening paragraph of the Constitution. Notice who is speaking in its very first words.
The Preamble is one long sentence. Find its subject: it starts with the word "We". Ask who "we" refers to.

The subject "We" is described in the first line, and the verb comes at the very end: "do ordain and promulgate this Constitution". The group named in the first line is the one that ordains it. Pick the choice that names that group.

solution.methodName: Find the provision, then match the key words

steps.action: Recall what the Preamble is: the one-sentence opening statement of the Constitution.
steps.why: "Preamble" means an opening statement. It says who made the Constitution and why.

steps.action: Find its subject. It opens: "We, the sovereign Filipino people, imploring the aid of Almighty God ..."
steps.why: "Sovereign" means holding the highest power. The Preamble says the people hold it.

steps.action: Find its verb at the end: "... do ordain and promulgate this Constitution."
steps.why: "Ordain and promulgate" means to set up and officially make known. The "We" at the start is the one doing this.

steps.action: The sovereign Filipino people ordain and promulgate the Constitution.

trapNotes.The Congress of the Philippines: Congress is created by the Constitution itself, in Article VI. The Preamble does not mention Congress. It speaks as "We, the sovereign Filipino people".
trapNotes.The President of the Philippines: The office of the President is set up in Article VII. The Preamble does not mention the President. It names the people.
trapNotes.The Supreme Court of the Philippines: The Supreme Court is created in Article VIII, Section 1, so it comes from the Constitution, not the other way around. The Preamble names the people.
